question: What does a user see when an agent/pre-step listener returns {kind:"reject"}? Written down as a measurement instead of an assumption.

probe.bundle: .tmp/prestep-probe (one inserted row, id probe-pre-step, name prestep-probe)
probe.listener: ctx.on('agent/pre-step', async (payload, next) => ({ kind: 'reject', reason })) — it owns the decision, so it does not chain next()

findings: A rejection opens the durable turn and then closes it as reason.kind = "blocked". There is no step/start, no user/message re-append, no assistant/* and no tool/call in the whole session.

The claimed batch is removed (removedCount 1, no inserted, no outcome: "canceled") — that is the claim being consumed, not a user cancellation. dsh-agent lanesForClaim treats "blocked" as an ending that accounts for the input, unlike "completed".
The typed message is therefore lost: a user who wants to retry has to type it again. That is the measured cost of a rejection.
The CLI exits 1, so a scripted caller can tell a refused turn from a completed one.
not_proven: The desktop UI render of reason.kind = "blocked" was not measured: the conversation definitions in this install contain no match on that reason, so what the window draws is unknown.
A rejection inside a multi-step turn (next-step steering) was not exercised; only the first proposed step of turn 1.
One profile, one provider route, one prompt.

verdict.reason: it neither pretends to succeed nor leaves a half-opened step; the turn ends in a named reason
verdict.because: the desktop rendering of "blocked" is unmeasured, and the input is discarded on rejection
